context: Naoko complains about a taxi traffic jam to Hina-young.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: ひな、今日、散々な道のりや!
lines.en: Hina, what a day! The roads were absolutely brutal!
lines.style: Loud, energetic Kansai drawl. Exasperated but affectionate — the kind of complaining that's half-performance. Throws her hands up on the opening. Quick pace, breathless.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: It really was crowded, wasn't it?
lines.style: Quiet, genuine. Eight years old but trying to sound grown-up and helpful. Soft in the chest — she's listening to her aunt more than speaking. Slight upward lift at the end, offering sympathy.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 殺到しとる、駅前、ピンチや!
lines.en: People everywhere at the station — what a mess!
lines.style: Sharper this time. Still Kansai-flavored but the frustration is real now. Punctuated, loud on 「殺到」. Energy driving forward. No laugh underneath it.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: 時計、ようけ気にしてますね。
lines.en: You keep checking the time, don't you?
lines.style: Observant, gentle. Not accusing — noticing. A child seeing an adult clearly. Soft and steady. The voice of someone who notices what people are really worried about.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: ハラ、ようけ立っとるわ!
lines.en: My feet are killing me after all that standing!
lines.style: Honest complaint, but wrapped in warmth and self-aware humor. A little surrender in it — she's tired and not hiding it. Kansai ease underneath. Slight laugh on herself.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: 到着、もう少しで、大丈夫!
lines.en: We're almost there — you'll be fine!
lines.style: Reassuring but not patronizing. Eight-year-old trying to be the adult in the moment. Warm, steady. A small hand placed on her aunt's arm. Genuine belief underneath.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: おう、ふだんから、覚悟しとるわ!
lines.en: Yeah, well — that's what you get used to when you do this kind of thing all the time!
lines.style: Softer now. A moment of philosophy and acceptance. Kansai warmth, not volume. Self-deprecating ease — she's made peace with her own exhaustion. Trailing off gently, like a quiet laugh at herself.
